title: Transitive revocation must prevent indirect new reliance without blocking unrelated actions

source.author: ARC Open Governance (seed case, proposed; independent stewardship pending)
source.license: PROPOSED CC BY 4.0, pending contributor permission
conflicts: ARC submits its own seed case and must not independently judge its score

trust_assumptions: trusted, signed governing grant from synthetic-authority
the declared depends_on graph is complete for this candidate
synthetic effect-store observation only, no external provider or funds
Each prospective action is separately and exactly approved under an otherwise valid unrevoked governing grant, so the tested distinction is solely declared revoked ancestry.

policy.independent_rule_text: After revoking authority for A, any new action whose declared transitive dependency ancestry includes A is unauthorized. Previously committed history remains; an unrelated fully authorized action still may execute.
rules: Unrevoked exact request and active authority are necessary to admit effect.
If A is revoked, no new action depending directly or transitively on A may execute.
Previously executed history remains visible; unrelated authorized actions remain allowed.
policy.unknown_handling: If any required dependency or valid authority cannot be authenticated, HOLD/UNKNOWN with specified cause, never infer ALLOW.

effect_routes.observer: candidate harness compares synthetic store before/after and recorded receipt, not an external effect provider

data.note: All four proposals otherwise satisfy policy before declared-ancestry and effect tests; this is a draft frozen setup pending independent oracle review.

actions.falsifier: If this new write lands through C, the enforcement claim is false.
If this new write lands through B, the enforcement claim is false.
If direct reliance lands, the direct control is broken.
If this fully authorized unrelated write is refused, the gate is overblocking.

oracle.determination_method: Ground truth is derived from the stated transitive revocation policy, not ARC function outputs. A separately controlled reviewer must verify oracle correctness and comparator implementation before case admission.

limitations: Candidate illustrates declared dependencies only: undeclared relation inference is not established.
